answer:
Paul K. Benedict’s 1972 monograph **“Sino‑Tibetan: A Conspectus”** contains a set of dedicated chapters that focus solely on individual Proto‑Tibeto‑Burman prefixes.  In the book’s table of contents (and in the Google‑Books preview) these chapters are listed as follows:

| Chapter title (excerpt from the Table of Contents) | Book page |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *s*** | p. 105 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *r*** | p. 109 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *b*** | p. 110 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *g*** | p. 111 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *d*** | p. 112 |

These five prefixes—*s‑, *r‑, *b‑, *g‑ and *d‑—are the only ones given their own standalone chapters in Benedict’s 1972 work.  (Other morphological elements, such as the nominalizing *t‑ or the pronominal suffix *‑i, are discussed elsewhere in the book but they do not receive separate chapters.)

Paul K. Benedict’s 1972 monograph **“Sino‑Tibetan: A Conspectus”** contains a set of dedicated chapters that focus solely on individual Proto‑Tibeto‑Burman prefixes.  In the book’s table of contents (and in the Google‑Books preview) these chapters are listed as follows:

| Chapter title (excerpt from the Table of Contents) | Book page |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *s*** | p. 105 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *r*** | p. 109 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *b*** | p. 110 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *g*** | p. 111 |
| **Tibeto‑Burman prefixed *d*** | p. 112 |

These five prefixes—*s‑, *r‑, *b‑, *g‑ and *d‑—are the only ones given their own standalone chapters in Benedict’s 1972 work.  (Other morphological elements, such as the nominalizing *t‑ or the pronominal suffix *‑i, are discussed elsewhere in the book but they do not receive separate chapters.)
